PASSO 1: Morgen fahre ich é o futuro de: STEP 1: everyday German future = present tense + a time word: «Morgen fahre ich nach Berlin» (I'm going to Berlin tomorrow). STEP 2: werden + infinitive at the end is for promises, predictions and assumptions. STEP 3: "going to" is NOT «gehen» + infinitive. STEP 4: the big false friend: «Ich will» means "I want", not "I will". "I will" is «Ich werde».

Werden: tornar-se e futuro, passo a pass: Werden: "become" and the future, step by step
PASSO 1: «werden» é irregular: ich werde: STEP 1: «werden» is irregular: ich werde, du wirst, er wird, wir werden, ihr werdet, sie werden. STEP 2: as a MAIN VERB, «werden» means TO BECOME, TO GET: «Es wird kalt» (it's getting cold), «Ich werde Lehrer» (I'm going to be a teacher — literally "I become a teacher"), «Er wird müde» (he's getting tired). STEP 3: as the future AUXILIARY, «werden» + infinitive at the END forms the FUTUR I: «Ich werde morgen arbeiten» (I will work tomorrow). STEP 4: the verb bracket again: «werden» in 2nd position and the infinitive at the end. STEP 5: question: «Wirst du kommen?» (Will you come?); negative: «Ich werde nicht kommen» (I won't come). STEP 6: with a separable verb, the whole infinitive goes to the end: «Ich werde früh aufstehen.»
o português usa o futuro simples («eu tr: English "will" + verb is the closest match ("I will work" = «Ich werde arbeiten»), but German uses it far less: most of the time, the present tense with «morgen», «nächste Woche» or «bald» does the job. And never confuse «werden» (will, become) with «wollen» (want): «Ich will kommen» = I want to come.

Quando usar o Futur I: When to use the Futur I
PASSO 1: na CONVERSA, o alemão usa muita: STEP 1: in CONVERSATION, German often uses the PRESENT tense with a time word for the future: «Morgen fahre ich nach Berlin.» That's completely natural — like English "I'm going to Berlin tomorrow". STEP 2: the «Futur I» appears for: (a) PROMISES and firm INTENTIONS: «Ich werde dir helfen» (I will help you); (b) PREDICTIONS: «Es wird morgen regnen» (it will rain tomorrow); (c) ASSUMPTIONS about the present, with «wohl», «wahrscheinlich»: «Er wird wohl krank sein» (he's probably sick — English "he'll be sick, I suppose"); (d) when there's no time word and the meaning requires it: «Wir werden sehen» (we'll see). STEP 3: if there's a time word (morgen, nächste Woche, bald), use the present. STEP 4: the Futur I goes well with «bestimmt», «wahrscheinlich», «wohl».
Morgen werde ich nach Berlin fahre.
With «morgen», the present tense is enough.

PASSO 1: para planos, use o presente com: STEP 1: for plans, use the present with a time word: «Nächste Woche fange ich einen Sprachkurs an» (next week I'm starting a language course). STEP 2: «wollen» expresses what you want: «Ich will Arzt werden» (I want to become a doctor). STEP 3: «werden» confirms the expected result: «Ich werde Arzt» (I'm going to be a doctor). STEP 4: «hoffen» and «glauben» help: «Ich hoffe, dass ich eine Stelle finde» (I hope I find a job). STEP 5: use «bald», «später», «irgendwann» to keep the timing vague.
